source.title: Global Status of Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems 2026

facts.interpretation: WMO reports 136 countries with multi-hazard early warning systems as of August 2026.
facts.limitation: Country-level system reporting is not a measure of every person's exposure to, receipt of, or ability to act on a warning.

facts.interpretation: WMO's key message states that 70 per cent of countries report having multi-hazard early warning systems.
facts.limitation: The summary page does not provide a country-by-country denominator table in the visible text; do not derive a denominator from this rounded percentage.

facts.interpretation: Fewer than half of reporting countries demonstrate capabilities across all four pillars.
facts.limitation: This is a country-level capability statement, not a population coverage or local warning-effectiveness rate.

facts.interpretation: WMO reports a 143 per cent increase in the number of countries reporting MHEWS since 2015.
facts.limitation: The percentage is source-reported; this snapshot does not independently reconstruct the 2015 baseline.

facts.interpretation: The WMO summary says more comprehensive systems are associated with lower disaster mortality and fewer people affected.
facts.limitation: Association is not a causal effect estimate; this summary does not justify attributing a specific avoided-loss amount to a local system.

supporting_sources.title: Early Warning Systems for mobile populations: Operational guidance
supporting_sources.claim: The guidance treats mobility as a persistent feature of risk and includes people temporarily present and people unable to move because of poverty, disability or insecurity.
